sections.text: Introduction

This document outlines the testing 
 procedure P1, which must be performed on a monthly bases
 as indicated by M1 in the above title 
 block

Deposits from plant for generating and using steam may reach the analyst in a 
variety of forms. They may be still attached to convex or concave surfaces of 
metal tubes or portions of plant, or they may already have been removed and put 
into suitable containers; they may be dry, wet, or oily; they may contain 
inclusions of old scale in a new matrix; they may show strata of deposits built 
up at different times in the history of the plant. In whatever form a deposit 
may come it shall be retained in its original form. The remainder shall then be 
available for analysis.
Summary of Analysis

This method covers the 
 manner in which the results of examination and analysis for inorganic 
 constituents of deposits formed from waters are to be reported.
Safety Precautions

items:
The sample must be taken as the applicable ASTM methods D 
 3370-76.

Acids such 
 as sulfuric acid and others are dangerous, so you have to wear breathing mask.

Keep these 
 acids closed. Do not get it in the eyes, on the skin, or on clothing. Do not 
 breathe them, use only in a hood.

Work To be Carried Out
Sampling and Analysis

History of Sample: 
Information regarding the source and history of the 
sample shall be included in the report of the analysis.
Name of company supplying sample.
Name and location of plant.
Date and time of sampling.
Number of sample.

Name and other designation of equipment from which 
sample removed.

Type of deposit, whether scale, sludge, or 
corrosion product.

Type of treatment applied to the water that formed 
the deposit.
Physical characteristics:

The physical characteristics of the sample. Such as 
color, form ( scaly, slimy, drusy ). Hardness, magnetic properties and structure 
( amorphous, crystalline ).
Preparation of Sample for Analysis:

Drying- Heat the deposit in an oven for one 
hour at 105 2C. The sample may have acquired moisture during grinding. 
Therefore dry 10-12 g. in a porcelain basin in an oven for one hour at 105 
 2C. Cool in a desiccator and bottle.

Note: Laminated specimens may, be separated 
into their component sections before drying.
Preparation of Oil Sample for Analysis:

Dissolve a small quantity of the sample in 3M 
HCl , and filter off any insoluble material on a sintered glass crucible.

Rinse the beaker with light petroleum ( boiling 
range 40-60C ) and wash the residue on the filter with this.

Keep this washed residue for the test for other 
organic matter.

Extract the filtrate and washings by shaking with 
light petroleum ( boiling range 40-60C ) in a separating funnel, removing the 
stopper from time to time to release any pressure.

Run off the aqueous layer, wash the light petroleum 
layer with distilled water, separate again and pour the light petroleum layer 
into a small beaker.

Evaporate the organic solvent on a hot-water bath 
in a fume cupboard. Observe if there is any appreciable residue.

For Organic Matter: Place about 0.5 g. of 
the sample on a porcelain crucible, heat gently at first and ignite more 
strongly later. Observe any charring or smoking which indicates the presence of 
organic matter.

The sample is now ready for analysis, and carry 
 out all analysis on the dried sample
Dissolving the Analytical Sample
Solution in Hydrochloric Acid:

This treatment will dissolve water-formed 
 deposits which do not contain a substantial percentage of stubborn components, 
 including calcium sulfate, various silicates, and some of the more refractory 
 spinals. The use of this solvent is advantageous in that it is not oxidizing, 
 and possible interference from sulfate or nitrate is not introduced.
Procedure

Weight 0.5 g of the analytical sample obtained, 
 into 250 mL beaker. Add 50 mL of HCl (1+4) and evaporate to dryness on a hot 
 plate contained in a hood. Add 10 mL of concentrated HCl and again evaporate 
 to dryness. Add 10 mL of concentrated HCl (1+9) bring to a boil, and separate 
 the solution by filtration through ash less filter paper.

Wash the residue and dilute the combined filtrate 
 and washings to a measured volume.

Aliquots of this solution shall be used for the 
 analysis of the constituents to be determined.

The residue may be retained for further 
 examination.

sections.text: Solution in Mixed Hydrochloric Acid-Nitric Acid:

This solvent is more effective in 
 eliminating traces of organic material and in dissolving more refractory 
 components which resist HCl alone.
Procedure

Add 5 mL of HNO3 to 0.5 g of the analytical 
 sample that has been weighed into 250 mL beaker and evaporate to 
 near dryness on a hot plate contained in a hood. Add 50 mL of dil.(1+1) HCl 
 and 5 mL of HNO3. Evaporate to dryness on a hot plate in a hood. Cool 
 and add 10 mL of HCl (1+1) acid and 1 mL of HNO3and repeat the 
 evaporation. Allow the beaker to cool and then add 50 mL of dil.(1+1) HCl. Boil 
 until the volume is decreased to approximately 25 mL and filter through 
 ash less filter paper.

Wash the residue and dilute the combined filtrate 
 and washings to a measured volume.

Aliquots of this solution shall be used for the 
 analysis of the constituents to be determined.

sections.text: Alkali Fusion:

This method of dissolving the sample is 
 especially useful for the rapid determinations of silica and aluminum.
Procedure

Add 9 sodium hydroxide pellets ( approximately 
 1.5 g ) to a 75 mL nickel crucible. Slowly heat the crucible over a meeker 
 burner until the pellets are molten. Allow the crucible and its contents to 
 cool to a room temperature.

Weigh 0.05 g of the analytical sample, and 
 transfer to the crucible containing NaOH. Reheat the crucible to remelt 
 the hydroxide and swirl to mix in the weighed material. Use a nickel wire or 
 rode to complete the mixing. Continue heating for 3 min after mixing, then 
 allow the melt to cool.

Add 50 mL of water to the crucible and stir 
 the contents of the crucible occasionally until the melt is 
 disintegrated completely (about 1 h).

Transfer the contents to a 1 liter volumetric 
 flask. Wash the crucible. Dilute to volume with water.

sections.text: Quantitative Analysis

Drying: 
Although the sample has been dried during 
preparation it may have acquired moisture during grinding. Therefore dry 10-12 g. 
in a porcelain basin in an oven at 105 2C for 1 hour. Cool in a desiccator and 
bottle. Carry out all analyses on the dried sample.
Oil

Weigh about 2 g. of the dried sample in a 50 ml 
beaker and transfer to a 500 mL separating funnel by the aid of about 20 mL of 
light petroleum boiling range 40-60C. Add 50 mL of water and then gradually add 
25 mL of HCl. Cool, if necessary, and shake well. Interrupt the shaking 
occasionally and release any pressure developed.

Allow to settle, then run off the lower layer into 
another separating funnel and carry out a second extraction with a further 10 mL 
light petroleum . Run off the lower layer and reject it.

Add the second light petroleum extract to the 
first, rinsing the separating funnel with a little light petroleum.

Wash the petroleum extract by shaking with 5 mL 
portions of water until free from acid.

Filter the extract through a dry ash less 
filter paper into a weighed 250 mL conical flask. Wash the paper 3 times with 5 
mL portions of light petroleum.

Remove the solvent from the filtrate and washings 
by evaporation on a water bath.

Add 3 drops of alcohol and dry in an oven 
controlled at 105 2C for 2 hours.

Loss on Ignition

Accurately weigh about 3 g. of the dried sample in 
a previously ignited, cooled and weighed platinum crucible. Heat gently for a 
few minutes and then strongly for 60 minutes in an electric furnace at 
approximately 1200C with occasional tapping to prevent caking. Cool in a 
desiccator and weigh. Repeat for a further 30 minutes and until the loss in 
weight between successive weightings does not exceed 40 mg.

sections.text: Reporting of Chemical Analysis

All data shall be reported as percentage by 
 weight of the dry sample.

For convenience in calculation, values for 
 oxides, acid anhydrides, and combined water may also be expressed on a basis 
 of chemical equivalents.

Value or relative equivalents. are obtained by 
 dividing each value of percentage by weight by the equivalent weight of the 
 respective oxide, acid radical, or water.

Quantitative determination shall be reported to 
 the nearest 0.1 %.

When a Quantitative determination is made and a 
 negative result is obtained, it shall be reported as "0,0".
